business_problem: Humana needed to reduce the cost and poor experience caused by an IVR that pushed too many provider calls to live agents for routine pre-service questions.
solution_summary: Humana worked with IBM Watson and IBM Data and AI Expert Labs & Learning to replace an underperforming IVR with a Provider Services Conversational Voice Agent that spans IBM Cloud and on-premises voice infrastructure. After a three-month proof of concept, the joint team combined multiple Watson applications in a single assistant, while watsonx Assistant for Voice handled the voice interaction layer at Humana. The system uses AI to determine caller intent, verify access rights and return eligibility, benefits, authorization, referral and other pre-service information without a live agent. Humana also trained seven language models and two acoustic models around different input types so the assistant could cope with healthcare terminology and noisy call-center conditions. In effect, the architecture turns provider phone inquiries into a continuously tuned voice workflow that serves routine healthcare administration at scale rather than handing those calls off to outsourced centers.

data_flow: Provider phone calls are processed by watsonx Assistant for Voice and custom speech models, IBM Watson interprets the intent and access rights for each call, and the system returns pre-service, eligibility, benefits, authorization or referral information without routing routine requests to a live agent.
business_outcome: The voice agent handles inquiries at about a third of the previous cost, delivers nearly double the response rate of the old IVR and lets providers complete common inquiries in about two minutes.
